newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - low sulphur cracked gets tighter.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - low sulphur cracked gets tighter.

text.p: Fuel oil retained its firm tone in northern Europe on Friday although activity was lmited.
Barges were pushed $2 a tonne higher to $120-121 fob ARA on the back of problems with prompt barrel supplies, but cargoes remained unchanaged around $120 cif NWE.

Support came from news that both Turkey and Portugal have tendered for up to 125,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel in December and January. But, the EdP tender of two plus one optional cargo was short of previous tenders and good supplies in the Med may limit the upside for NWE prices.
Russian straight-run fuel continues to shadow the cracked market and despite market rumours there has been no conclusive announcement from Moscow regarding a long-expected export tariff.

The low sulphur cracked market was firm with strong U.S. natural gas prices giving support to a tight market. Only a 22-25kt cargo is available for early December lifting with a 45-50kt parcel not coming onto the market until the second half of Dec.
An Italian buyer picked up a 40kt Donges cargo at a quotes related price for "promptish" loading.
